TEST TREE RESULTS (local machine, all against the real helper plist, each with its own bootout + confirmed absence): A (env scrub + wrapper + cwd, no setsid) exit 0; B (full env + os.setsid) exit 0; C (all four spawn attributes combined) exit 0; D1 (the complete daemonkit sequence bootout → enable → bootstrap from an interactive shell) exit 0, enable writing nothing and poisoning nothing. NINE mechanisms now falsified on this machine: key presence, .app-standalone, DB wedge, teardown window, setsid alone, env scrub+cwd+stdio, all-four-combined, the enable step, and the full sequence from an interactive shell. The enable theory's cross-machine correlation (every recorded failure had enable in the chain, every success skipped it) did not survive the direct test.

SOLE SURVIVING CANDIDATE: process identity / responsibility attribution. Every success in the record descends from an Orca-hosted zsh (__CFBundleIdentifier=com.stablyai.orca — a real app-bundle identity); every failure descends from brew → Cellar-resident codesigned capt-hookd. Consistent with the unexplained asymmetry (plain-exe keyless agents bootstrap fine under daemonkit; the GUI .app agent never does — only .app agents need LaunchServices/BTM registration). Open hole in the theory: macOS responsibility normally propagates down the process tree from the hosting app, so brew's grandchildren should carry Orca/terminal responsibility unless the signed Cellar capt-hookd re-anchors it — needs macOS-internals verification, not more shell tests.

NEXT PROBE (gated, running): TEST E — unified-log capture (launchd, launchctl, backgroundtaskmanagementd, lsd, com.apple.xpc.launchd subsystem, debug level) during a deliberately-triggered failing brew postinstall. launchd's own log at the EIO moment should name the refusal reason directly — the black-box variable isolation is exhausted; this reads the box's label. If the log names it, that is the root-cause verdict; if silent at debug level, the identity test (Terminal.app-parented vs responsibility-disclaimed caller) is the next design and the work moves fully into daemonkit code + macOS research.
